checkpoints.description: [1/1] Record the /compact request's usage. compactSession calls the provider with memo:false, so it bills, but it recorded no llm.usage event: the tokens reached no usage total, no Usage panel figure and no budget, which is the same defect already fixed for the in-loop summary.

impact_assessment.why: A billed request that leaves no record makes every usage total and every budget wrong by an amount nobody can see.
impact_assessment.benefits: Usage totals, the Usage panel and any spend report include /compact, so the numbers add up.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: llm.usage gains purpose compact and runId null for a request outside a run; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: one extra usage event per compact
impact_assessment.mitigation: Priced through the same priceStep as every request; the test asserts the exact arithmetic and is mutation-tested

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Pin tool reachability. The registry in tools.ts and the live profile toolNames in harness.ts are separate lists, so a tool added to one and not the other is invisible to the model. Probed end to end: all 16 registered tools are exposed and the four background-shell tools work through executeTool, so the state was correct but unpinned. Added a test for both halves.

impact_assessment.why: A capability that exists in the registry and is unreachable is the same failure shape as a parameter that is advertised and ignored.
impact_assessment.benefits: Adding a tool without exposing it now fails a test instead of shipping silently unreachable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: The guard is mutation-tested by removing the background tools from the profile, and the dispatch half drives a real task start to kill

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Calibrate the perf gate to the host. The gate failed repeatedly on an untouched tree; the loaded samples were internally consistent (1-18% spread) but shifted upward, so a spread threshold could not help, which I proved by building one and testing it against the observed numbers (it caught none). Replaced it with a fixed CPU workload unrelated to atelier, measured at 187.9-194.4 ms (3.4% spread), recorded as calibrationMs and divided out of both the budget and the baseline comparison.

impact_assessment.why: An absolute millisecond budget is a statement about how busy the computer is; the same untouched tree measured 3.49 ms and 18.63 ms on different runs.
impact_assessment.benefits: A slow host is allowed proportionally more time and a real regression still fails, so the gate says something about the code.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: baseline schema 2 gains calibrationMs; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: baselines record their own calibration
impact_assessment.mitigation: Verified in both directions with the real script: 2x and 5x host references pass, a tightened 0.5 ms budget still fails and names the host-equivalent limit

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/1] Verified in both directions with the real script: a reference calibration set 2x faster yields hostScale 2.09 and the same raw numbers pass; 5.23x passes; a budget genuinely tightened to 0.5 ms still fails and names the host-equivalent limit. 4 unit tests pin the arithmetic, 121 test files green.

measurements.workload: budget set to 0.5 ms on a 1.05 host

checkpoints.description: [plan] Open a task for the two commits made after atelier-perf-calibration closed: the gate-role clarification (bf959e7) and its ADR. The ledger flagged them as unverified commits following a completed task, which is correct process feedback: I committed code after closing the task that should have owned it.

[1/1] State the perf gate's two roles in the code: the host-calibrated absolute budget is the verdict, and the baseline comparison fails only past max(1.5x, baseline plus six baseline MADs). Records why a candidate-spread guard was tried and rejected (at six MADs it would absorb 7.98ms on a 3.66ms metric, a gate that never fails), and why sub-50% drift cannot be enforced from three passes on a shared host.

impact_assessment.why: One gate run still failed after calibration at hostScale 1.05; measuring showed the ledger stat costs 0.02ms, direct dispatch measures 4.06ms, and a re-run of identical code gave 3.66ms with 0.04 MAD against the failing run's 1.33 MAD. Same code, different samples.
impact_assessment.benefits: A reader can see which check is binding and which is advisory, and the gate cannot silently become a rubber stamp.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Verified the gate still fails a real regression by tightening the budget to 0.5ms: ok False with the host-equivalent limit named

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Share the host calibration and apply it to agent-bench, which compared raw mean latency against a baseline recorded on whatever the machine was doing at the time. Extracted scripts/hostCalibration.ts (calibrateHost, hostScale, HOST_REFERENCE_MS), pointed agent-perf at it, and made agent-bench record calibrationMs (schema 2) and divide the candidate latency by the ratio before comparing.

impact_assessment.why: agent-bench failed twice on an untouched tree for the same reason agent-perf did: absolute milliseconds measure the computer.
impact_assessment.benefits: Both perf gates now compare host-equivalent numbers, and the calibration exists in one place with its own tests.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: agent-bench baseline schema 1 to 2, and a schema-1 baseline is still read (scale 1, raw comparison); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: baselines carry their calibration
impact_assessment.mitigation: Verified by halving the baseline calibration: hostScale 1.93 and the candidate mean halved to 52.55 before comparison, so the scaling is real

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/1] Verified: halving the bench baseline's calibrationMs produced hostScale 1.93 and halved the candidate mean to 52.55 before comparison; restoring it returned hostScale to 1. agent-perf and agent-bench share one calibration, both baselines carry it, 8 unit tests cover the helper, and 122 test files are green.
